1.1: Aight, so these the words Moses told all Israel while they was still on this side of the Jordan, out in the wilderness, in the valley near Suph, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
1.2: From Horeb to Kadesh Barnea, if you walk straight, it's just an eleven-day trip by way of Mount Seir.
1.3: But check this—it wasn't till the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses finally spoke on everything the Lord told him to tell Israel.
1.4: This was after they took down Sihon, the Amorite king in Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
1.5: So now, Moses was on this side of the Jordan, in Moab, breaking everything down and explaining the Law, saying:
1.6: The Lord our God told us at Horeb: "Aight y'all, y'all been camped out at this mountain long enough."
1.7: It's time to pack up and move out—head to the hill country of the Amorites, hit up all the lands around there: the valley, the mountains, the lowlands, the desert, and the coast—Canaanite land, all the way up to Lebanon, to the big River Euphrates.
1.8: Look, I already set the land up for y'all! Go ahead, take what's yours—this the same land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying I'd give it to them and their kids after them.
1.9: Then I told y'all back then: 'Look, I can't handle all y'all by myself no more.'
1.10: The Lord your God has multiplied y'all—look at you now! You as many as the stars in the sky.
1.11: And I pray the Lord, the God of your fathers, make y'all even a thousand times bigger and bless y'all just like He promised.
1.12: But for real, how I'm supposed to handle all y'all issues, complaints, and drama by myself?
1.13: So here's what we gon' do: Y'all pick some wise, understanding, and knowledgeable folks from your tribes, and I'll put them in charge.
1.14: And y'all was like, "Yeah, that sound like a solid plan."
1.15: So I picked out leaders from y'all's tribes—some over thousands, some over hundreds, fifties, and tens—plus other officials to keep things in order.
1.16: Then I told them judges: "Listen up—when folks come to y'all with problems, be fair. Don't matter if it's between family or an outsider, judge it right."
1.17: Ain't no favoritism in justice—rich or poor, everybody gets a fair shot. And don't be scared of nobody, 'cause God is the real Judge. If a case too tough, bring it to me, and I'll handle it.
1.18: And that's when I laid out everything y'all needed to do.
1.19: So we left Horeb and rolled through that big, scary wilderness, just like God told us to. Then we got to Kadesh Barnea.
1.20: And I told y'all, "Aight, we here. These the Amorite mountains—this the land God is giving us."
1.21: Look, God already set this up for us! Go take it! Don't be scared, don't get shook!
1.22: But then y'all came to me saying, "Hold up, let's send some dudes ahead first to scope out the land and let us know the best way to roll up in there."
1.23: I thought it was a good idea, so I picked twelve men, one from each tribe.
1.24: They went up, checked the land, and came back with a report from the Valley of Eshcol.
1.25: They even brought some fruit back and said, "Yo, this land is good! This exactly what God promised us!"
1.26: But y'all ain't wanna hear it. Instead, y'all straight up rebelled against God's order.
1.27: Y'all started complaining in your tents, talking about, "God don't love us! He brought us outta Egypt just to get us wiped out by the Amorites!"
1.28: Y'all was shook, saying, "The people there way bigger and taller than us! The cities are huge with walls up to the sky! We even saw the Anakim giants there!"
1.29: Then I told y'all, "Stop being scared! Don't trip!"
1.30: God Himself gon' fight for y'all, just like He did back in Egypt.
1.31: Y'all seen how God took care of us in the wilderness—He was carrying us like a father carries his kid all the way to this place.
1.32: But even after all that, y'all still ain't trust the Lord your God.
1.33: He was leading y'all the whole time—showing y'all the way in a fire by night and a cloud by day.
1.34: So when God heard y'all acting like this, He was heated and made a promise, saying:
1.35: "Ain't none of this evil generation gon' step foot in that good land I promised y'all's ancestors—"
1.36: —Except Caleb! He gon' get his share, 'cause he followed God with his whole heart.
1.37: Even I ain't getting in, 'cause of y'all.
1.38: But Joshua? He gon' lead y'all in, so encourage him, 'cause he got the job now.
1.39: And y'all's kids, the same ones y'all thought would be victims? They the ones that gon' inherit the land.
1.40: But as for y'all? Turn around. Head back toward the Red Sea.
1.41: Then y'all tried to flip it, saying, "We messed up! We gon' go fight just like God said!" So y'all grabbed y'all weapons, ready to roll up the mountain.
1.42: But the Lord said to me, "Tell them not to go. I ain't with them, and they gon' lose."
1.43: I told y'all, but y'all ain't listen. Instead, y'all ran up in there, thinking y'all could handle it anyway.
1.44: And what happened? The Amorites came out swinging like a swarm of bees, chasing y'all from Seir all the way to Hormah.
1.45: Y'all came back crying to God, but He wasn't listening.
1.46: And that's how y'all ended up stuck in Kadesh for a long time.

2.1: Then we turned back and headed into the wilderness, toward the Red Sea route, just like the Lord told me. We kept circling around Mount Seir for a long time.
2.2: Then the Lord came through and told me:
2.3: 'Aight, y'all been going in circles around this mountain long enough—turn north now.'
2.4: 'Tell the people: "Y'all about to pass through the land of Esau's descendants—y'all's own relatives—who live in Seir. They gon' be shook when they see y'all rolling up, so be careful."'
2.5: 'Don't start nothing with them, 'cause I ain't giving y'all none of their land—not even a single footstep. I gave Mount Seir to Esau's people, that's their inheritance.'
2.6: 'If y'all need food, buy it. If y'all thirsty, buy water. Pay for what you take.'
2.7: 'The Lord your God been blessing y'all this whole time. He see the struggle y'all been through, trekking through this big ol' wilderness. For forty years, He been right there with y'all, and y'all ain't lacked a thing.'
2.8: So when we left Esau's people in Seir, we stayed off their main road, passing by Elath and Ezion Geber, and then we went toward the Moab wilderness.
2.9: Then the Lord told me: 'Don't mess with Moab or pick no fights with them. I ain't giving you none of their land, 'cause I gave Ar to Lot's descendants to keep.'
2.10: (Back in the day, the Emim used to live there—they was huge like the Anakim.)
2.11: (People used to call them giants, same as the Anakim, but the Moabites called them Emim.)
2.12: (The Horites used to live in Seir too, but Esau's descendants ran them out and took their land, just like Israel later did with the land the Lord gave them.)
2.13: Then the Lord told us: 'Aight, get up and cross the Valley of Zered.' So we did.
2.14: From Kadesh Barnea to the time we finally crossed Zered, 38 years passed—enough time for that whole generation of warriors to die off, just like the Lord said would happen.
2.15: God's hand was against them the whole time, wiping them out from the camp, till they was all gone.
2.16: And when the last of them was gone,
2.17: The Lord spoke to me again, saying:
2.18: 'Today, y'all gon' cross over Ar, the edge of Moab.'
2.19: 'When y'all get near Ammon, don't mess with them or try to take their land. I ain't giving y'all none of it, 'cause I already gave it to Lot's descendants.'
2.20: (That land used to belong to the Zamzummim, another group of giants like the Anakim.)
2.21: (They was big, many, and strong, but the Lord wiped them out so Ammon's people could take the land.)
2.22: (Same thing He did for Esau's descendants in Seir, taking out the Horites so they could settle there.)
2.23: (Even the Avim, who lived near Gaza, got taken out by the Caphtorim who moved in after them.)
2.24: Then the Lord told us: 'Get up, get moving, and cross the Arnon River. Look, I already handed over Sihon, king of the Amorites in Heshbon, to y'all. Go take his land—go to war!'
2.25: 'Starting today, every nation under heaven gon' hear about y'all and be scared. They gon' be shook just hearing y'all coming.'
2.26: So I sent messengers from Kedemoth wilderness to King Sihon of Heshbon, trying to keep the peace.
2.27: I told him: 'Let us pass through your land. We ain't gon' touch nothing, just sticking to the road.'
2.28: 'We'll buy food and water—just let us walk through on foot.'
2.29: 'That's what Esau's people in Seir and the Moabites in Ar did for us, so we just tryna get across to the land the Lord our God giving us.'
2.30: But Sihon wasn't having it. The Lord made his spirit stubborn, and he refused to let us pass, 'cause God had already planned to hand him over to us.
2.31: Then the Lord told me: 'Look, I already started giving Sihon's land to you. Go take it—it's yours now.'
2.32: So Sihon came out with his whole army, ready to fight us at Jahaz.
2.33: But the Lord our God gave him to us—we took him down along with his sons and all his people.
2.34: We took all his cities and wiped them out completely—men, women, kids—nobody was left.
2.35: Only thing we kept was the livestock and the spoils from the cities we conquered.
2.36: From Aroer (on the banks of the Arnon River) all the way to Gilead, no city was strong enough to stop us. The Lord handed them all over to us.
2.37: But we stayed clear of the Ammonite land—the Jabbok River, the hill country, and anywhere else the Lord told us not to go.

3.1: Then we headed up the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came out with his whole crew, ready to throw hands at Edrei.
3.2: But the Lord told me: 'Don't even trip. I already gave him and his whole army to you—same way I did with Sihon, king of the Amorites in Heshbon. Handle him just like you handled Sihon.'
3.3: So the Lord our God delivered Og into our hands, along with his people, and we fought till none of them was left standing.
3.4: We took all his cities—not a single one was left. Sixty cities, the whole Argob region, the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan.
3.5: These wasn't no small villages either—every city had high walls, gates, and strong bars. Plus, there was a whole bunch of smaller towns.
3.6: We completely wiped them out, just like we did to Sihon, king of Heshbon. Every man, woman, and child—gone.
3.7: But we kept all the livestock and the goods from the cities for ourselves.
3.8: So at that time, we took the whole land from the two Amorite kings on this side of the Jordan—from the Arnon River up to Mount Hermon.
3.9: (The Sidonians call Mount Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
3.10: We took all the cities in the plains, all of Gilead, all of Bashan, up to Salcah and Edrei, which were in Og's kingdom.
3.11: Og was the last of the giants. His bed? Made of iron. You can still see it in Rabbah of Ammon. It was 9 cubits long and 4 cubits wide—that's over 13 feet long!
3.12: So at that time, we split up the land: From Aroer, near the Arnon River, to half of Gilead and its cities—I gave it to the Reubenites and Gadites.
3.13: The rest of Gilead, plus all of Bashan, Og's old kingdom, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh. (This whole area, Argob and Bashan, was known as the land of giants.)
3.14: Jair, son of Manasseh, took all of Argob up to the borders of Geshur and Maacah. He renamed Bashan after himself—Havoth Jair—and that's what they still call it.
3.16: To the Reubenites and Gadites, I gave land from Gilead to the Arnon River (the middle of the river was the border), and up to the Jabbok River, which bordered Ammon.
3.17: Their land included the Jordan Valley, from Chinnereth (Sea of Galilee) down to the Salt Sea, all the way to the slopes of Pisgah.
3.18: Then I told y'all: 'The Lord your God gave y'all this land to keep. But all y'all strong fighters need to cross over armed and ready to fight alongside your Israelite brothers.'
3.19: 'Your wives, kids, and livestock (and I know y'all got a lot of livestock) can stay behind in the cities I gave y'all.'
3.20: 'But once the Lord gives them rest and they got their own land across the Jordan, then y'all can go back to your own land.'
3.21: Then I told Joshua: 'You saw with your own eyes what the Lord did to these two kings. That's exactly what He gon' do to every kingdom you about to face.'
3.22: 'Don't be scared of them—the Lord your God is fighting for you.'
3.23: Then I begged the Lord at that time, saying:
3.24: 'Lord God, You already been showing Your power to me. Ain't no other god in heaven or earth that can do what You do.'
3.25: 'Please, let me cross over and see the good land on the other side of the Jordan—the mountains and Lebanon.'
3.26: 'But the Lord was mad at me because of y'all, and He ain't wanna hear it. He told me, "That's enough! Don't bring this up again."'
3.27: 'Go up to the top of Pisgah and look around—north, south, east, west—but you ain't crossing this Jordan.'
3.28: 'Instead, put Joshua in charge, encourage him, and strengthen him, 'cause he gon' lead these people into the land and help them take it.'
3.29: So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.

4.1: Aight, listen up, Israel—pay attention to these rules and judgments I'm teaching y'all, so y'all can live and go take the land the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
4.2: Don't add nothing to what I'm telling you, and don't take nothing away. Just follow the commands the Lord your God gave you.
4.3: Y'all saw with your own eyes what the Lord did at Baal Peor—how He wiped out all the men who followed that false god.
4.4: But y'all who stayed loyal to the Lord your God? Y'all still standing today.
4.5: I gave y'all these laws and rules, straight from the Lord my God, so y'all can follow them in the land y'all about to take.
4.6: Stick to them carefully—'cause when other nations hear about these laws, they gon' say, 'Dang, this is a wise and understanding nation!'
4.7: What other nation got a God this close to them? Whenever we call on the Lord, He right there!
4.8: And what other nation got laws this fair like the ones I'm giving y'all today?
4.9: So be real careful—don't forget what y'all seen. Keep it in your heart forever, and teach it to your kids and grandkids.
4.10: Remember when y'all stood before the Lord at Mount Horeb? He told me, 'Gather the people, I'ma speak to them so they learn to fear Me and teach their kids to do the same.'
4.11: Y'all came to the mountain, and it was burning with fire all the way up to the sky—covered in dark clouds and smoke.
4.12: Then the Lord spoke outta the fire. Y'all heard His voice, but y'all ain't see no form—just His words.
4.13: He gave y'all His covenant, the Ten Commandments, and wrote them on two stone tablets.
4.14: And the Lord told me to teach y'all these laws, so y'all can follow them once y'all take the land.
4.15: So listen—be real careful. Y'all ain't see no physical form when God spoke to y'all out the fire at Horeb.
4.16: Don't go acting up and making idols of any kind—no statues of men, women, animals, or birds.
4.17: No statues of anything walking the earth or birds flying in the sky.
4.18: No statues of anything crawling or any fish in the water.
4.19: And don't go looking up at the sun, moon, or stars and thinking you gotta worship them. The Lord put them up there for everybody, not just y'all.
4.20: But y'all different—the Lord pulled y'all outta Egypt (that iron furnace) to be His own people.
4.21: Now, the Lord was mad at me 'cause of y'all, and He swore I ain't crossing the Jordan to the good land He's giving y'all.
4.22: I gotta stay here and die, but y'all gon' cross over and take the land.
4.23: So be careful—don't forget the Lord's covenant and don't go making idols, 'cause He already told y'all not to do that.
4.24: The Lord your God is a consuming fire—He's jealous and won't share y'all with no fake gods.
4.25: If y'all start acting up after y'all settle in the land—making idols and doing what's evil—
4.26: I'm telling y'all right now: Heaven and earth are my witnesses—y'all ain't gon' last in this land. Y'all gon' be destroyed.
4.27: The Lord gon' scatter y'all to other nations, and only a few of y'all gon' be left where He sends you.
4.28: There, y'all gon' be stuck worshiping fake gods—nothing but wood and stone that can't see, hear, eat, or smell.
4.29: But if y'all start looking for the Lord with your whole heart and soul, y'all gon' find Him.
4.30: When trouble hits and all this happens in the future, if y'all turn back to the Lord and listen to Him—
4.31: He gon' be merciful. He won't abandon you, He won't destroy you, and He won't forget the covenant He made with your ancestors.
4.32: Look back through history—from the time God made humans to now—has anything like this ever happened?
4.33: Have any other people heard God's voice from fire like y'all did—and survived?
4.34: Has any god ever come through and snatched a whole nation outta another one—using miracles, signs, war, power, and fear—like the Lord did for y'all in Egypt?
4.35: God showed y'all this so y'all know He alone is God—ain't nobody else like Him.
4.36: He let y'all hear His voice from the sky so y'all could learn, and He showed y'all His fire on earth—His words came from the flames.
4.37: 'Cause He loved y'all's ancestors, He chose y'all, freed y'all from Egypt with His own power,
4.38: And He drove out stronger nations ahead of y'all, just to give y'all their land as an inheritance—just like He promised.
4.39: So today, y'all better understand this: The Lord alone is God—up in heaven and down on earth—ain't nobody else.
4.40: So keep His laws and commands, so things go well for you and your kids, and y'all live long in the land the Lord is giving y'all forever.
4.41: Then Moses set apart three cities on this side of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
4.42: These cities were safe zones for anyone who accidentally killed someone without meaning to—so they could escape and live.
4.43: Bezer (for Reuben's tribe), Ramoth in Gilead (for Gad's tribe), and Golan in Bashan (for Manasseh's tribe).
4.44: This is the law Moses gave to Israel—
4.45: The commands, testimonies, and rules he told them after they left Egypt.
4.46: He gave these laws on this side of the Jordan, near Beth Peor, in the land they took from Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Israel had defeated him after leaving Egypt.
4.47: They also took land from Og, king of Bashan—two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, where the sun rises.
4.48: From Aroer (near the Arnon River) to Mount Hermon,
4.49: And all the land east of the Jordan down to the Sea of the Arabah, below the Pisgah hills.

5.1: Then Moses called all Israel together and said: 'Listen up, Israel! These the rules and laws I'm laying down today. Learn them and make sure y'all follow them!'
5.2: The Lord our God made a covenant with us back at Mount Horeb.
5.3: This wasn't just for our ancestors—it's for us, the ones alive right now.
5.4: The Lord spoke directly to y'all, face to face, from the fire on the mountain.
5.5: I had to stand between y'all and the Lord back then, 'cause y'all was too scared to go up the mountain. And this what He said:
5.6: I am the Lord your God, the One who brought y'all outta Egypt, outta slavery.
5.7: Y'all bet not put no other gods before Me.
5.8: Don't go making any idols—no statues, no images of anything in the sky, on the ground, or in the water.
5.9: Don't bow down to them, don't serve them. I'm a jealous God, and I hold people accountable for their sins—even three and four generations down for the ones who hate Me.
5.10: But for those who love Me and keep My commands, I show mercy for a thousand generations.
5.11: Don't be out here using the Lord's name carelessly. The Lord ain't gon' let that slide.
5.12: Keep the Sabbath day holy, just like the Lord told you.
5.13: Do all your work in six days.
5.14: But on the seventh day, it's the Lord's rest day. That mean no working—not you, not your kids, not your workers, not even your animals or any outsiders in your land. Everybody rests.
5.15: And don't forget—y'all used to be slaves in Egypt, and the Lord freed y'all with His mighty power. That's why He told y'all to keep the Sabbath.
5.16: Respect your father and mother, just like the Lord commanded, so you can live long and blessed in the land He's giving you.
5.20: Don't lie on your neighbor in court.
5.21: Don't be out here lusting after your neighbor's wife. Don't be jealous of their house, land, servants, ox, donkey, or anything that belongs to them.
5.22: That's what the Lord told y'all straight from the fire, the clouds, and the darkness—in a loud voice. He didn't add nothing else. Then He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
5.23: When y'all heard God's voice out the fire and smoke, and saw the mountain blazing, all the tribe leaders and elders came to me.
5.24: Y'all said: 'The Lord really showed up today! We heard His voice and survived!'
5.25: But if this fire keeps burning, we gon' die! If we hear God's voice again, we ain't gon' make it.
5.26: Ain't no human ever heard God speak outta fire like we just did and lived. Who else has experienced this?
5.27: Moses, you go talk to Him. Listen to what He say, then come back and tell us. We'll listen and do whatever He says.
5.28: The Lord heard what y'all said and told me: 'I heard them loud and clear, and honestly, they right.'
5.29: I just wish they would always have this kind of heart—to fear Me and keep My commandments, so things will go well for them and their kids forever.
5.30: Now, go tell them: 'Go back to y'all's tents.'
5.31: But you, Moses, stay here with Me. I'ma give you all the commandments, laws, and rules so you can teach them how to live in the land I'm giving them.
5.32: So listen—do exactly what the Lord told y'all. Don't turn left or right.
5.33: Walk in the path the Lord set, so you can live long, be blessed, and stay in the land He's giving y'all.

6.1: Aight, listen up—this the commandment, these the rules and laws the Lord your God told me to teach y'all, so y'all can follow them once y'all step into this new land.
6.2: You gotta respect the Lord, keeping all His commands—you, your kids, and your grandkids—for as long as y'all live. Do that, and y'all gon' live long and prosper.
6.3: So listen, Israel! Follow what He said, so things go well for y'all. The Lord promised your ancestors He'd make y'all multiply big time and give y'all a land flowing with milk and honey.
6.4: Listen up, Israel! The Lord our God is the one and only God!
6.5: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength.
6.6: Keep these words I'm giving you deep in your heart.
6.7: Teach them to your kids—talk about them at home, on the road, when you lay down, and when you get up.
6.8: Tie them to your hands, keep them in front of your eyes like a reminder.
6.9: Write them on your doorposts and gates—make sure His words stay in your face.
6.10: Now when the Lord your God brings you into this promised land—the one He promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—He gon' give y'all big, beautiful cities that y'all ain't even build.
6.11: Y'all gon' get houses full of good stuff y'all ain't put there, wells y'all ain't dig, vineyards and olive trees y'all ain't plant. And when y'all eat and get full—
6.12: Be careful! Don't forget the Lord who brought y'all out of Egypt, out of slavery.
6.13: Respect the Lord and serve Him only—when y'all make promises, let it be in His name.
6.14: Don't chase after other gods—them false gods the people around you worship.
6.15: The Lord your God is jealous—if y'all start acting up, His anger gon' come down hard and wipe y'all off the face of the earth.
6.16: Don't be out here testing the Lord like y'all did back at Massah.
6.17: Stick to the Lord's commands—follow His rules and laws like He told you.
6.18: Do what's right in the Lord's eyes, so things go well for you, and you can take the good land He promised your ancestors.
6.19: The Lord gon' clear out your enemies so y'all can settle in the land—just like He said.
6.20: One day, your kid gon' ask, 'What all these laws, rules, and judgments mean? Why God tell us to follow them?'
6.21: Tell them: 'We used to be slaves in Egypt, but the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand.'
6.22: 'He hit Egypt with signs and wonders, put Pharaoh and his whole house through it—and we saw it all with our own eyes.'
6.23: 'Then He brought us out so He could bring us in—to give us this land He promised our ancestors.'
6.24: 'That's why the Lord told us to keep these commands—so we'd stay blessed, stay safe, and stay alive.'
6.25: 'And if we stay on track, following all His commands, that's what makes us righteous in God's eyes.'

7.1: When the Lord your God brings y'all into this land He's giving you, He gon' clear out a bunch of nations before y'all—Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—seven nations that's bigger and stronger than y'all.
7.2: And when the Lord your God hands them over to you, y'all gotta take them down completely. Don't make no deals with them, and don't be out here showing mercy.
7.3: Don't marry into their families—don't give your daughters to their sons, and don't take their daughters for your sons.
7.4: 'Cause if you do, they gon' pull your kids away from Me and make them worship other gods. That's gon' set off God's anger, and He gon' wipe y'all out quick.
7.5: This how you handle them—tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their idol poles, and burn up their carved images.
7.6: Y'all are a set-apart people—holy to the Lord your God. He chose y'all to be His own special treasure, outta everybody else on the earth.
7.7: He ain't pick y'all 'cause y'all was the biggest nation—y'all was actually the smallest.
7.8: But He loved y'all, and He kept the promise He made to your ancestors. That's why He brought y'all out of Egypt, with a mighty hand, and set y'all free from Pharaoh.
7.9: So know this—the Lord your God is real. He keeps His word and shows love for a thousand generations to those who love Him and follow His commands.
7.10: But if somebody hates Him, He gon' pay them back to their face and destroy them. He ain't gon' hold back.
7.11: So stick to His commands, His laws, and His rules—do what He said today.
7.12: If y'all listen and obey these commands, the Lord your God gon' keep His covenant with you, just like He promised your ancestors.
7.13: He gon' love you, bless you, and make you multiply. He gon' bless your kids, your crops, your grain, your wine, your oil, your animals—all of it in the land He's giving y'all.
7.14: Y'all gon' be blessed more than any other nation—won't be no barren men or women, and even your animals gon' reproduce.
7.15: The Lord gon' keep y'all healthy—He ain't gon' put none of those terrible diseases from Egypt on you. But He gon' hit your enemies with them instead.
7.16: The Lord gon' hand your enemies over to you, and y'all gotta take them out. Don't feel sorry for them, and don't mess with their gods, 'cause that's just gon' trap you.
7.17: Now, if y'all start thinking, 'Man, these nations way stronger than us—how we supposed to defeat them?'
7.18: Don't be scared. Just remember what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and all of Egypt.
7.19: Remember the crazy signs and wonders, the plagues, and how God brought y'all out with power. That's exactly what He gon' do to all these nations y'all worried about.
7.20: The Lord gon' send hornets after them until the ones who try to hide get wiped out.
7.21: Don't be shook—the Lord your God is mighty and powerful and He's right there with you.
7.22: The Lord gon' clear them out little by little—He ain't gon' do it all at once, 'cause if He did, the wild animals might overrun the land before y'all settle in.
7.23: But don't worry—He gon' deliver them into your hands and make sure they get completely destroyed.
7.24: He gon' hand their kings over to you, and you gon' wipe out their whole legacy—nobody gon' be able to stand against y'all.
7.25: Burn up their idols and destroy their false gods. And don't try to keep the silver or gold on them, 'cause that's just gon' trap you—it's disgusting to the Lord.
7.26: Don't bring none of that cursed stuff into your house, or you gon' be cursed just like it. Destroy it completely—hate it, reject it, and get rid of it, 'cause it ain't nothing but trouble.

8.1: Every single command I'm giving y'all today? Make sure you follow it, so you can live, grow, and take over the land the Lord promised your ancestors.
8.2: And don't forget—the Lord your God led y'all through the wilderness for 40 years to humble y'all and test what's really in your hearts. He wanted to see if y'all would stay loyal to His commandments or not.
8.3: He made y'all go hungry, then fed y'all manna—something neither y'all nor your ancestors ever seen before. He did that to teach y'all that man don't live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the Lord.
8.4: Think about it—y'all clothes never wore out, and your feet ain't swell up after 40 years of walking!
8.5: So understand this—just like a father disciplines his son, that's how the Lord your God corrects y'all.
8.6: That's why y'all gotta stay faithful, keep His commandments, walk in His ways, and respect Him.
8.7: The Lord your God is about to take y'all into a good land—a land with streams, fountains, and fresh water flowing from the valleys and hills.
8.8: A land filled with wheat, barley, grapevines, fig trees, pomegranates, olive oil, and honey—
8.9: A land where food ain't ever gon' run out. Y'all ain't gon' be lacking nothing. The land even got iron in the rocks and copper in the hills.
8.10: So when y'all eat good and get full, don't forget to bless the Lord for the good land He gave you.
8.11: Be careful! Don't forget the Lord your God by ignoring His commands, rules, and laws that I'm giving y'all today.
8.12: 'Cause when y'all eat good, build nice houses, and settle down,
8.13: And when your animals, money, and everything else starts multiplying,
8.14: Watch yourself! Don't get prideful and forget the Lord—the One who brought y'all out of Egypt, outta slavery.
8.15: He led y'all through that dangerous desert, full of poisonous snakes, scorpions, and dry land with no water. And He brought water outta a rock just to keep y'all alive.
8.16: He fed y'all manna in the wilderness—something y'all's ancestors ain't ever seen before—to humble and test y'all, so He could bless y'all in the end.
8.17: But don't get it twisted—don't start thinking, 'I did this myself. My strength and hustle got me all this wealth.'
8.18: Nah, remember the Lord your God—He's the one who gives y'all the power to get wealth, to keep His promise to your ancestors, just like He said.
8.19: If y'all forget the Lord and start following other gods, worshiping and serving them, I'm telling y'all right now—y'all gon' be wiped out.
8.20: Just like the nations the Lord destroys before y'all, that's exactly how y'all gon' go down if y'all don't listen to the Lord your God.

9.1: Listen up, Israel! Y'all about to cross the Jordan today and take land from nations bigger and stronger than you—cities with walls that reach the sky.
9.2: The people there? Tall and powerful—the Anakim. Y'all already heard folks say, 'Ain't nobody messing with the Anakim!'
9.3: But understand this—the Lord your God is going ahead of y'all like a consuming fire. He gon' wipe them out, knock them down, and y'all gon' take them out quick, just like He said.
9.4: But don't get cocky after the Lord pushes them out—don't be out here saying, 'It's 'cause I'm so righteous that God gave me this land.' Nah, it ain't about you. It's 'cause them nations wicked.
9.5: It's not 'cause y'all so righteous or pure-hearted. It's 'cause these nations wilding out so bad that the Lord gotta remove them. Plus, He keeping His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
9.6: So get this straight—the Lord ain't giving y'all this land 'cause y'all so holy. Y'all been hard-headed since day one!
9.7: Don't forget how y'all kept making the Lord mad all through the wilderness. Since y'all left Egypt, y'all been rebelling against Him.
9.8: At Horeb, y'all made the Lord so mad He almost wiped y'all out.
9.9: I went up the mountain to get the stone tablets—the covenant the Lord made with y'all. I was up there 40 days and nights, no food, no water.
9.10: Then the Lord gave me two stone tablets written by His own hand—everything He told y'all from the fire on the mountain.
9.11: After 40 days, He gave me the tablets—the very covenant between y'all and Him.
9.12: Then the Lord told me, 'Hurry up! Get down there—your people done messed up big time. They already turned from My ways and made an idol.'
9.13: The Lord also said, 'I've been watching these folks—they hard-headed.'
9.14: 'Moses, step aside and let Me wipe them out. I'ma erase them from history and start over with you, making a nation bigger and better than them.'
9.15: So I went down the mountain, carrying the two stone tablets in my hands, and the mountain was still on fire.
9.16: When I saw what y'all did—y'all made a golden calf, turned from God real quick—
9.17: I threw the tablets down and broke them right in front of y'all.
9.18: Then I fell on my face before the Lord, just like the first time—40 days and nights, no food, no water, begging Him not to destroy y'all for your sins.
9.19: I was scared of how mad the Lord was—He was ready to wipe y'all out. But He listened to me that time too.
9.20: The Lord was even about to take out Aaron—but I prayed for him too.
9.21: Then I burned that golden calf, smashed it, ground it up to dust, and threw the dust in the river.
9.22: And let's not act like that was the only time y'all made God mad. At Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth Hattaavah, y'all did the same thing!
9.23: And at Kadesh Barnea, when the Lord said, 'Go take the land I'm giving you,' y'all refused. Y'all didn't trust Him, didn't listen—straight-up rebelled.
9.24: Since I first met y'all, y'all been rebelling.
9.25: So I fell on my face before the Lord for 40 days and nights, 'cause He said He was about to wipe y'all out.
9.26: I begged Him, 'Lord, don't destroy the people You saved with Your mighty power. They belong to You.'
9.27: 'Remember Your servants—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Don't focus on how stubborn and sinful these people are.'
9.28: 'If You destroy them, Egypt gon' say, "God couldn't finish what He started, so He just wiped them out in the wilderness."'
9.29: 'But Lord, they Your people. You brought them out with Your mighty power and Your strong arm.'

10.1: Then the Lord told me, 'Cut out two more stone tablets, just like the first ones, and bring 'em up the mountain. Also, make a wooden chest to hold them.'
10.2: 'I'm gon' write the same words on these new tablets that was on the ones you broke. Then you gon' put them inside the ark.'
10.3: So I made an ark outta acacia wood, cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and climbed back up the mountain with them in my hands.
10.4: And just like before, the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them—same words He spoke to y'all from the fire on the mountain that day y'all gathered. Then He gave them to me.
10.5: I came down the mountain, put the tablets inside the ark I made, just like the Lord told me, and they still there.
10.6: (Now, after that, the Israelites moved from Bene Jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried. His son Eleazar took over as high priest.)
10.7: (From there, we traveled to Gudgodah, then to Jotbathah, a place with rivers of water.)
10.8: (It was during that time that the Lord set the Levites apart—they the ones who carry the ark of the covenant, serve before the Lord, and bless people in His name, and they still do it today.)
10.9: (That's why the Levites ain't got no land like the other tribes—their inheritance is the Lord Himself, just like He promised.)
10.10: Just like before, I stayed up on the mountain for 40 days and 40 nights. The Lord heard me again and decided not to destroy y'all.
10.11: Then He told me, 'Get up and lead the people forward, so they can take the land I swore to give their ancestors.'
10.12: Aight, Israel, what's the Lord really asking from y'all? Just this—fear Him, walk in His ways, love Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul.
10.13: Follow His commands and rules, 'cause they ain't just for Him—they for your own good.
10.14: Look, everything belongs to the Lord—heaven, the highest heavens, and the whole earth.
10.15: But even with all that, He chose y'all's ancestors and set His love on them. And now, He picked y'all, their descendants, to be His own special people.
10.16: So stop being so stubborn—circumcise your hearts! Get rid of that hard-headedness.
10.17: The Lord your God is the realest of all—King of kings, Lord of lords. He's mighty, awesome, and He don't play favorites or take bribes.
10.18: He makes sure orphans and widows get justice. He loves foreigners and makes sure they got food and clothes.
10.19: So y'all gotta love the foreigners too, 'cause y'all was foreigners in Egypt once.
10.20: Fear the Lord, serve Him, stick close to Him, and swear by His name only.
10.21: He's the One you should praise—your God, the One who did all these amazing things y'all saw with your own eyes.
10.22: Your ancestors went down to Egypt as just 70 people, and now look at y'all—the Lord done multiplied y'all like the stars in the sky.

11.1: So love the Lord your God, and keep His rules, laws, and commands—not just sometimes, but always.
11.2: Listen, I ain't talking to y'all's kids—the ones who ain't seen firsthand how the Lord disciplines, how powerful He is, and how He moves with a mighty hand.
11.3: They ain't see the miracles He pulled off in Egypt—how He shut Pharaoh down and flipped Egypt upside down.
11.4: They ain't see how He drowned the Egyptian army—horses, chariots, everything—in the Red Sea when they was chasing y'all. That army? Still gone to this day.
11.5: They ain't live through how God kept y'all in the wilderness till y'all got here.
11.6: Or how He handled Dathan and Abiram—y'all remember? The earth straight up opened its mouth and swallowed them, their families, their tents, and everything they owned right in front of everybody.
11.7: But y'all? Y'all saw all this with your own eyes.
11.8: So keep every command I'm giving y'all today, so y'all can stay strong, take the land, and actually hold on to it.
11.9: Do this, and y'all gon' live long in the land the Lord promised your ancestors—a land flowing with milk and honey.
11.10: This land ain't like Egypt, where y'all had to work the ground, water it by hand, and struggle like it was a backyard garden.
11.11: Nah, this land got hills and valleys—it gets water straight from the heavens.
11.12: God Himself watches over this land from the start of the year to the very end.
11.13: So if y'all truly obey what I'm telling you—love the Lord, serve Him with all your heart and soul—
11.14: He gon' send rain in its season—early rain, late rain—so y'all can grow grain, grapes, and olives.
11.15: He gon' make sure the fields stay full of grass for y'all's animals, and y'all gon' have plenty to eat.
11.16: Watch yourselves! Don't let your hearts get twisted and start chasing other gods and worshiping them.
11.17: If y'all do, the Lord gon' shut the heavens up, no rain gon' fall, the land gon' dry up, and y'all gon' be wiped out quick from this good land He gave you.
11.18: Keep these words locked in your heart and soul. Tie them on your hands, wear them like a badge on your forehead.
11.19: Teach them to your kids—talk about them at home, on the road, when you wake up, and when you go to bed.
11.20: Write them on your doorposts and gates—keep them in front of you at all times.
11.21: Do this, and y'all and y'all's kids gon' live long in the land the Lord promised, as long as the sky is over the earth.
11.22: If y'all faithfully keep all these commands—love the Lord, walk in His ways, stay close to Him—
11.23: Then the Lord gon' drive out every nation in front of you, even the ones that look bigger and badder than y'all.
11.24: Everywhere y'all step? That's yours. From the desert to Lebanon, from the Euphrates River to the Western Sea—it's all y'all's territory.
11.25: Ain't nobody gon' be able to stand against y'all. The Lord gon' make sure everybody fears you wherever y'all step—just like He promised.
11.26: Look, I'm laying out two choices for y'all today—a blessing and a curse.
11.27: The blessing comes if y'all obey the Lord's commands I'm giving you today.
11.28: The curse happens if y'all ignore His commands and start chasing other gods y'all don't even know.
11.29: When the Lord brings y'all into this land, y'all gon' declare the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
11.30: These mountains are on the other side of the Jordan, in Canaan, where the sun sets, near Gilgal by the great oak trees of Moreh.
11.31: Y'all about to cross the Jordan and take the land the Lord is giving y'all. And once y'all got it, y'all gon' settle in it.
11.32: But listen, y'all better follow all the laws and rules I'm setting in front of y'all today.

12.1: These the rules and laws y'all gotta follow once y'all step into the land the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving y'all. Stick to them as long as you live.
12.2: Y'all gotta completely destroy all the places where the nations before y'all used to worship their false gods—on the mountains, hills, and under shady trees.
12.3: Tear down their altars, smash their pillars, burn up their wooden idols, cut down their statues, and wipe out their names from history.
12.4: Don't worship the Lord like they worship their gods. That ain't how He want it.
12.5: Instead, look for the place the Lord chooses from among y'all's tribes—the spot where He puts His name. That's where y'all need to go.
12.6: Bring y'all's burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, special offerings, freewill gifts, and firstborn livestock there.
12.7: Celebrate in the Lord's presence—you, your family, everybody—because of the blessings He gave y'all.
12.8: Don't do whatever you feel like, like y'all been doing out here in the wilderness.
12.9: 'Cause right now, y'all ain't reached the peace and inheritance the Lord got waiting for y'all.
12.10: But once y'all cross the Jordan, settle in the land the Lord is giving you, and He gives y'all rest from y'all's enemies so y'all can live safely—
12.11: Then He gon' choose a place for His name to dwell, and that's where y'all gotta bring y'all's offerings, tithes, and special gifts.
12.12: And that's where y'all gon' rejoice before the Lord—you, your kids, your servants, and even the Levites, 'cause they ain't got no land like the rest of y'all.
12.13: Don't just offer sacrifices anywhere you see fit.
12.14: Only offer them where the Lord tells you, in the place He chooses from one of y'all's tribes.
12.15: Now, you can eat meat wherever you live, however much you want, as long as the Lord blesses you with it—clean and unclean folks alike can eat it, just like y'all eat gazelle and deer.
12.16: But don't eat the blood—pour it out on the ground like water.
12.17: Don't eat your tithes at home—whether it's grain, wine, oil, or the firstborn of your flock. And don't eat your vowed and freewill offerings there either.
12.18: Eat those in the Lord's presence at the place He chooses—you, your family, your servants, and the Levites. Celebrate the blessings He gave you.
12.19: And don't forget the Levites! Take care of them as long as you in the land.
12.20: When the Lord expands your borders like He promised and you get a craving for some meat, go ahead and eat as much as you want.
12.21: If the place the Lord chose is too far, you can slaughter animals from your own flock at home and eat all you want.
12.22: Same way you eat gazelle and deer, you can eat this—clean or unclean folks alike.
12.23: But don't eat the blood, 'cause the blood is life.
12.24: Pour it out on the ground like water.
12.25: Don't eat it, so things go well for you and your kids when you do what's right in the Lord's eyes.
12.26: But when it comes to the holy offerings and vows, take those to the place the Lord chooses.
12.27: Offer the sacrifices on the Lord's altar, pour the blood on it, and then eat the meat.
12.28: Follow these commands carefully, so things go well for you and your kids forever when you do what's right in the Lord's sight.
12.29: When the Lord drives out the nations before you, and y'all take their land and settle in it—
12.30: Don't get caught up in their ways! Don't start wondering, 'How did these folks worship their gods? Maybe we should do the same?'
12.31: No! Don't worship the Lord like they worship their false gods, 'cause they did disgusting things He hates—they even burned their own kids as sacrifices.
12.32: Stick to what I commanded y'all. Don't add to it, and don't take nothing away.

13.1: If a so-called prophet or dreamer pops up and starts showing signs or wonders—
13.2: And even if what they predict comes true, but then they say, 'Let's go worship other gods that you ain't never known before'—
13.3: Don't listen to them! The Lord your God is just testing you, trying to see if you really love Him with all your heart and soul.
13.4: Stick with the Lord—respect Him, follow His commands, listen to His voice, and serve Him with all you got.
13.5: That so-called prophet or dreamer gotta go. Put them to death, 'cause they tried to lead you away from the Lord, the same God who brought you out of Egypt and freed you from slavery. Get rid of that evil among y'all.
13.6: Even if it's your own brother, your son, daughter, wife, or closest friend, and they secretly try to get you to worship other gods—
13.7: Whether it's gods from nearby nations or far away lands that neither you nor your ancestors ever knew about—
13.8: Don't listen to them! Don't try to protect them, don't cover for them, and don't show them mercy.
13.9: They gotta be put to death, and you gotta be the first one to do it, followed by the rest of the people.
13.10: Stone them until they die, because they tried to pull y'all away from the Lord, the same God who saved you from Egypt.
13.11: This gon' make the rest of Israel take note and think twice before trying that foolishness again.
13.12: If y'all hear rumors that in one of the cities the Lord gave y'all, some folks been saying—
13.13: 'A few shady people started convincing others to go serve other gods that we ain't never known'—
13.14: Y'all better investigate! Check the facts, ask questions, and make sure the story is true.
13.15: If it turns out that they really did pull people into idol worship, then you gotta wipe that city out completely.
13.16: Gather all its stuff into the middle of the street, then burn the whole place down as an offering to the Lord. Leave it in ruins—forever.
13.17: Don't keep nothin' from that city! If y'all handle business, the Lord will turn away His anger, show y'all mercy, and bless y'all even more, just like He promised.
13.18: But you gotta stay obedient, listening to the Lord and keeping all His commands, doing what's right in His eyes.

14.1: Y'all are God's children—so don't be out here cutting yourselves or shaving your heads for the dead like the other nations do.
14.2: The Lord set y'all apart—y'all His chosen people, His special treasure out of everybody on earth.
14.3: Don't eat nothing nasty or detestable.
14.4: Here's what's good to eat: ox, sheep, goat,
14.5: Deer, gazelle, roe deer, wild goat, mountain goat, antelope, and mountain sheep.
14.6: If an animal got split hooves and chews cud, y'all can eat it.
14.7: But some animals chew cud but don't have split hooves—like the camel, rabbit, and rock hyrax—don't eat them! They unclean to y'all.
14.8: Same with pigs—yeah, they got split hooves, but they don't chew cud. Don't eat them, don't even touch their dead bodies.
14.9: In the water, only eat fish with fins and scales.
14.10: Anything that don't got fins and scales? That's nasty, don't eat it.
14.11: All clean birds are good to eat.
14.12: But don't eat these: eagles, vultures, buzzards,
14.15: More owls, jackdaws, vultures, fisher owls,
14.17: Any insect that flies and crawls? Nope. Don't eat that either.
14.18: But all the clean birds? Y'all can eat those.
14.19: Don't eat anything that died by itself. You can give it to a foreigner, but y'all set apart for the Lord.
14.20: And don't be out here boiling a baby goat in its mama's milk.
14.21: Don't eat anything that died naturally. You can give it to foreigners or sell it to strangers, but y'all are a holy people to the Lord your God.
14.22: Make sure you tithe—set aside a tenth of your crops every year.
14.23: Take it to the place the Lord chooses—bring your grain, wine, oil, and firstborn animals and eat before Him. This way, y'all always remember to respect the Lord.
14.24: Now, if the place is too far and you can't carry all that—
14.25: Sell it, take the money, and go to the Lord's chosen place.
14.26: Then buy whatever you want—oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink—whatever your heart wants. Eat before the Lord and celebrate with your family.
14.27: And don't forget the Levites, 'cause they ain't got no land like y'all do.
14.28: Every third year, take a tenth of your harvest and store it up in your town.
14.29: The Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows—anybody who ain't got land—can come and eat till they full. Then the Lord gon' bless all the work you do.

15.1: Every seven years, y'all gotta cancel debts.
15.2: Here's how it works—if you lent somebody something, you gotta let it go. Don't go chasing them down for it, 'cause this is the Lord's release.
15.3: Foreigners? You can still collect from them, but when it comes to your own people, wipe the debt clean.
15.4: If everybody doing right, ain't gon' be no poor folks among y'all anyway, 'cause the Lord gon' bless you big time in the land He's giving you.
15.5: But that's only if y'all actually listen to the Lord and follow His commands carefully.
15.6: If you do, the Lord gon' bless you just like He promised—y'all gon' be lenders, not borrowers. Y'all gon' rule over nations, but ain't nobody gon' rule over you.
15.7: If there's somebody struggling in your community, don't be cold-hearted or stingy with them.
15.8: Open your hand and help them out—give them what they need.
15.9: And don't start thinking, 'Man, the seventh year almost here, I ain't tryna lend them nothing just for the debt to get canceled.' That kind of thinking is wicked. If you let them suffer, they gon' cry out to the Lord, and that's gon' be on you.
15.10: Be generous, and don't be mad about it. When you do, the Lord gon' bless all your work and everything you touch.
15.11: Truth is, there's always gon' be poor folks. That's why I'm telling y'all—always be ready to help your people.
15.12: If one of your own people, a Hebrew man or woman, works as a servant for six years, in the seventh year, they go free.
15.13: And when they leave, don't send them off empty-handed.
15.14: Hook them up with stuff from your flock, your crops, and your wine—give them some of the blessings the Lord gave you.
15.15: Remember, y'all was slaves in Egypt before the Lord freed you. That's why I'm telling y'all to do this.
15.16: But if your servant says, 'I don't wanna leave—I love it here, y'all treat me like family'—
15.17: Then you take an awl (a sharp tool) and pierce their ear at the door, making it official. They gon' stay with you for life. Same goes for female servants.
15.18: And don't trip about letting them go, 'cause they worked for you twice as hard as a hired worker for six years. The Lord gon' bless you for doing right.
15.19: All firstborn male animals from your herd and flock? Set them apart for the Lord. Don't work your firstborn ox, and don't shear your firstborn sheep.
15.20: Take it to the place the Lord chooses, and eat it with your family before the Lord every year.
15.21: But if the animal got a defect—if it's lame, blind, or messed up in any way—don't sacrifice it.
15.22: Instead, y'all can eat it at home—clean or unclean folks alike—just like you would with deer or gazelle.
15.23: But don't eat the blood—pour it out on the ground like water.

16.1: When the month of Abib comes around, keep the Passover for the Lord your God, 'cause that's when He brought y'all out of Egypt at night.
16.2: Sacrifice the Passover from your flock and herd at the place the Lord chooses to put His name.
16.3: Don't eat leavened bread with it. For seven days, eat unleavened bread—the bread of struggle—'cause y'all left Egypt in a hurry. This way, y'all always remember the day the Lord brought y'all out.
16.4: No leaven should be found anywhere in your land for seven days. And don't let any of the Passover meat from the first night stay till morning.
16.5: You can't just sacrifice the Passover anywhere in your land.
16.6: You gotta do it at the place the Lord chooses at twilight, right when the sun is going down—just like when y'all left Egypt.
16.7: Roast the meat and eat it at the Lord's chosen place. Then, in the morning, go back to your tents.
16.8: For six days, eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day, have a sacred assembly to the Lord. No work on that day.
16.9: Start counting seven weeks from the time you start harvesting your crops.
16.10: Then celebrate the Feast of Weeks, bringing a freewill offering according to how much the Lord has blessed you.
16.11: Rejoice before the Lord! You, your kids, your servants, the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows—everybody needs to celebrate at the place the Lord chooses.
16.12: And don't forget—y'all used to be slaves in Egypt. So make sure you obey these rules.
16.13: For seven days, celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles after you finish harvesting your crops and making your wine.
16.14: Rejoice! You, your kids, your servants, the Levites, the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows—everybody joins in!
16.15: Keep this sacred feast for seven days at the place the Lord chooses, 'cause He gon' bless your harvest and all the work you do. So go ahead and celebrate hard.
16.16: Three times a year, every man gotta show up before the Lord at the place He chooses—for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles. And don't show up empty-handed.
16.17: Everybody should bring an offering, giving whatever they can, based on how much the Lord has blessed them.
16.18: Set up judges and officials in every city the Lord gives you, and make sure they judge fairly.
16.19: Don't twist justice—don't play favorites or take bribes, 'cause bribes blind even the wise and mess up fair rulings.
16.20: Stick to real justice, so y'all can live long and hold on to the land the Lord is giving you.
16.21: Don't plant no trees as idols near the Lord's altar.
16.22: And don't set up sacred pillars—the Lord hates those things.

17.1: Don't offer no janky sacrifices—if an animal got a defect or any blemish, don't bring it to the Lord. That's disrespectful to Him.
17.2: If somebody in your community—man or woman—starts wildin' out, breaking the Lord's covenant—
17.3: If they start worshiping other gods, like the sun, the moon, or the stars—things the Lord ain't never told them to follow—
17.4: And word gets out about it, y'all better look into it carefully. If it turns out to be true and that kind of evil really went down in Israel—
17.5: Then that person gotta go. Take them out to the gates and stone them to death.
17.6: Don't execute nobody off one person's word. You need at least two or three witnesses to confirm it.
17.7: The witnesses gotta be the first ones to throw the stones, then everybody else joins in. That way, y'all remove the evil from among you.
17.8: If y'all got a case that's too complicated—whether it's about murder, legal disputes, or punishments—and y'all can't figure it out,
17.9: Then take it to the priests and judges at the place the Lord chooses. Let them make the call.
17.10: Whatever they decide, follow it exactly—don't do your own thing.
17.11: Stick to the judgment they give you. Don't stray left or right—just do what they say.
17.12: If somebody refuses to listen to the priest or the judge, that person gotta die. Y'all gotta get rid of that arrogance in Israel.
17.13: When the people see this, they gon' learn their lesson and stop trying to act above the law.
17.14: When y'all finally settle in the land the Lord is giving you and y'all say, 'We want a king like the other nations,'
17.15: Then make sure it's a king the Lord chooses. He gotta be one of your own—don't put some foreigner in charge over you.
17.16: The king can't be out here stacking up horses, especially not from Egypt, 'cause the Lord already told y'all, "Don't go back there."
17.17: He can't be stacking up wives either, 'cause that'll pull his heart away from the Lord. And he better not be hoarding gold and silver for himself.
17.18: When he becomes king, he needs to write out a copy of this law straight from the priests.
17.19: He gotta keep that law with him and read it every day, so he learns to respect the Lord and follow all His commands.
17.20: This gon' keep him humble—so he don't start thinking he better than his people or start twisting the law to his own benefit. If he follows it, he and his family gon' stay in power for a long time.

18.1: The priests and Levites—the whole tribe of Levi—ain't got no land inheritance like the rest of Israel. They live off the offerings made to the Lord.
18.2: They don't get no land to own, 'cause the Lord Himself is their inheritance, just like He promised.
18.3: This what belongs to the priests from the sacrifices the people bring—whether it's a bull or a sheep—they get the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.
18.4: They also get the firstfruits of y'all's grain, wine, oil, and the first cut of sheep's wool.
18.5: The Lord picked them specifically to serve in His name—them and their descendants—forever.
18.6: If a Levite moves from his hometown and comes to the place the Lord chooses, wanting to serve—
18.7: He can serve just like the other Levites who are already there standing before the Lord.
18.8: He gets an equal share, besides any money he gets from selling his personal property.
18.9: When y'all get into the land the Lord is giving y'all, don't be out here copying the nasty ways of these other nations.
18.10: Don't let nobody be out here sacrificing their kids in fire, practicing witchcraft, sorcery, reading omens, or fortune-telling.
18.11: No spells, no calling on spirits, no mediums, no trying to talk to the dead.
18.12: Anybody who does these things is disgusting to the Lord. That's why He getting rid of these nations before y'all.
18.13: Y'all gotta be different—fully committed to the Lord.
18.14: These other nations out here listening to fortune-tellers and sorcerers—but the Lord ain't set that up for y'all.
18.15: The Lord your God gon' raise up a prophet like me—somebody from among y'all's own people. Y'all need to listen to him.
18.16: This the same thing y'all asked for back at Mount Horeb, when y'all said, 'We can't handle hearing God's voice directly or seeing His fire—we'll die!'
18.17: The Lord said, "They right about that."
18.18: So He gon' raise up a prophet, just like Moses, from y'all's own people. He gon' put His words in that prophet's mouth, and the prophet gon' speak exactly what God commands.
18.19: Anybody who refuses to listen to the words God speaks through that prophet? They gon' answer to God Himself.
18.20: But if some fake prophet comes out here talking like the Lord told him something when He didn't, or if they speak in the name of other gods—that prophet gotta die.
18.21: If y'all wondering, "How do we know if God really spoke through this prophet?"
18.22: It's simple—if what they say don't happen, then God ain't say it. That prophet just running their mouth, and y'all ain't gotta be scared of them.

19.1: When the Lord your God clears out these nations and gives you their land, and y'all settle down in their cities and houses—
19.2: Set aside three cities in the middle of the land the Lord is giving you.
19.3: Build good roads leading to them and divide the land into three sections, so anybody who needs to escape can get there quick.
19.4: Here's how it works—if somebody accidentally kills their neighbor without meaning to, they can run to one of these cities and be safe.
19.5: Like if two folks go out to the woods to chop trees, and one swings an axe but the head flies off and hits the other person, killing them—that wasn't on purpose.
19.6: The person who caused it needs a safe place to run before the victim's family comes after them for revenge. Otherwise, in their anger, they might kill them even though it wasn't murder.
19.7: That's why I'm telling y'all—set up three cities for this.
19.8: If the Lord expands y'all's territory like He promised and gives you more land—
19.9: And if y'all stay obedient to His commands, loving the Lord and walking in His ways—then y'all need to add three more cities to the first three.
19.10: That way, innocent blood won't be shed in the land the Lord is giving you, and y'all won't be guilty of murder.
19.11: But if somebody actually hates their neighbor, sets them up, kills them, and then tries to run to a city of refuge—
19.12: The elders from their hometown need to go get them and hand them over to the victim's family.
19.13: No mercy—y'all gotta get rid of the guilt of murder in Israel so everything stays right.
19.14: Don't go moving your neighbor's property markers that were set by the ancestors. The Lord is giving y'all this land—respect the boundaries.
19.15: One witness ain't enough to convict somebody of a crime. You need at least two or three witnesses to prove it.
19.16: If somebody comes forward lying on someone else, trying to frame them—
19.17: Both of them need to stand before the Lord, in front of the priests and judges.
19.18: The judges gotta investigate carefully, and if they find out the witness was lying—
19.19: Then that liar gets the same punishment they was tryna put on the innocent person. That's how y'all keep evil out of the community.
19.20: Everybody else gon' hear about it and think twice before lying on somebody again.
19.21: No pity. If the crime is serious, the punishment gotta match—life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

20.1: When y'all go to war and see the enemy got more soldiers, horses, and chariots than you—don't be scared! The Lord your God is with you, the same one who brought y'all out of Egypt.
20.2: Before the battle starts, the priest gon' come up and talk to the people.
20.3: He gon' say: 'Listen up, Israel! Today y'all facing the enemy. Don't get weak-hearted, don't be scared, don't panic.
20.4: The Lord your God is right there with y'all— He gon' fight for you and give you the victory!'
20.5: Then the officers gon' step up and ask the people, "Anybody just built a new house and ain't had time to dedicate it? Go back home—don't die in battle and let somebody else enjoy your house."
20.6: "Anybody plant a vineyard but ain't got to eat from it yet? Go home—don't die and let another man eat your crops."
20.7: "Anybody engaged to a woman but ain't married her yet? Go home—don't die in battle and let another man take your wife."
20.8: Then they gon' ask, "Anybody scared? If so, go back home so you don't discourage the others."
20.9: After that, they gon' set up captains to lead the army into battle.
20.10: When y'all roll up on a city to fight, first offer them a chance for peace.
20.11: If they accept, don't destroy them. They gon' live under you and serve y'all.
20.12: But if they don't wanna make peace and wanna fight instead—then go ahead and besiege the city.
20.13: When the Lord hands the city over to you, take out all the men with the sword.
20.14: But the women, kids, animals, and everything else in the city? That's y'all's to keep. Take the plunder the Lord is giving you.
20.15: This is what y'all do for cities that ain't part of the land God is giving you—the ones far away.
20.16: But for the cities in the land the Lord is giving you? Don't leave nothing breathing.
20.17: Wipe out the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—just like the Lord told you.
20.18: If y'all leave them alive, they gon' teach y'all their evil ways, leading y'all into sin against the Lord.
20.19: When y'all at war for a long time, don't go cutting down the city's fruit trees. Those trees give food—they ain't your enemy.
20.20: But if a tree don't give food? You can cut those down to build weapons and siege ramps until the city falls.

21.1: If somebody gets killed and left out in a field, and nobody knows who did it—
21.2: The elders and judges gotta go out and measure the distance from the body to the closest cities.
21.3: Whichever city is closest to the crime scene, its elders gotta take a young cow that's never been worked or used for plowing.
21.4: They gotta take it down to a valley with flowing water—somewhere that ain't been farmed—and break its neck there.
21.5: Then the priests (Levites) come through, 'cause they the ones God picked to handle blessings and settle disputes.
21.6: After that, the elders of the closest city gotta wash their hands over the dead cow's body.
21.7: And they gotta say, "We ain't spill this blood, and we ain't see who did."
21.8: "Lord, forgive us—your people, Israel. We innocent. Don't hold us accountable for this." Then the Lord gon' clear them of guilt.
21.9: That's how y'all keep the land clean from innocent blood—by doing what's right in God's eyes.
21.10: When y'all go to war, and the Lord hands the enemy over to you—
21.11: If you see a beautiful woman among the captives and wanna marry her—
21.12: Bring her home, let her shave her head and trim her nails.
21.13: Give her a full month to grieve for her parents. After that, she becomes your wife.
21.14: But if later you change your mind, you gotta let her go free. Don't sell her or treat her like a slave, 'cause you already humbled her.
21.15: If a man got two wives, and he loves one more than the other, but the unloved wife gives birth to his firstborn—
21.16: When he splits his inheritance, he can't ignore the true firstborn just 'cause his mama ain't his favorite.
21.17: He gotta give the firstborn son his rightful double portion, 'cause that's his first strength. That's just how the rules go.
21.18: If a man got a stubborn, rebellious son who won't listen to his parents, even after they discipline him—
21.19: His parents gotta take him to the city elders at the city gate.
21.20: And they gotta say, "This our son—he's rebellious, don't listen, greedy, and a drunk."
21.21: Then the men of the city gotta stone him to death. That's how y'all get rid of evil and make sure everybody else gets the message.
21.22: If somebody commits a crime that deserves the death penalty, and they get executed and hung on a tree—
21.23: Don't leave their body up overnight. Bury them the same day, so the land don't get cursed. A person hung on a tree is cursed by God.

22.1: If you see your brother's ox or sheep wandering off, don't just ignore it— go get it and bring it back to him.
22.2: If you don't know who it belongs to, take care of it at your house until he comes looking for it. Then give it back.
22.3: Same thing goes for his donkey, his clothes, or anything else he lost. Don't act like you ain't see it.
22.4: If you see your brother's donkey or ox struggling and fallen, don't just walk away—help him lift it back up.
22.5: A woman shouldn't be out here wearing men's clothes, and a man shouldn't be out here dressing like a woman. The Lord ain't rocking with that.
22.6: If you find a bird's nest—whether in a tree or on the ground—with the mama sitting on her eggs or babies, don't take the mama with them.
22.7: Let the mama go and take only the babies. That way, you'll be blessed and live long.
22.8: If you build a house, make sure you put a safety railing around the roof, so you don't bring guilt on yourself if somebody falls off.
22.9: Don't plant different kinds of seeds in your vineyard— it'll mess up your crops and ruin the harvest.
22.10: Don't plow with an ox and a donkey tied together— that ain't right.
22.11: Don't wear clothes made of mixed fabrics— like wool and linen together.
22.12: Make sure your clothes got tassels on the four corners—that's how y'all stay reminded of God's laws.
22.13: If a man marries a woman, but then decides he don't want her anymore, claiming she wasn't a virgin—
22.14: And he spreads rumors about her, bringing shame to her name—
22.15: Then her parents gotta bring proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate.
22.16: Her father has to say, 'I gave my daughter to this man, and now he tryna ruin her name.'
22.17: Then they show the proof, and the elders gotta punish the man.
22.18: He gotta pay her father 100 shekels of silver for bringing shame on an innocent woman, and he can't ever divorce her.
22.19: They'll fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give it to the girl's father, 'cause he put dirt on a virgin of Israel's name. Plus, she gotta stay his wife—he can't ever divorce her as long as he live.
22.20: But if it turns out he was telling the truth, and she wasn't a virgin—
22.21: Then she gets taken to her father's house, and the men of the city stone her to death—because she played the harlot in her father's house. That's how y'all get rid of evil.
22.22: If a man sleeps with another man's wife, both of them gotta die. Get rid of the evil from Israel.
22.23: If a man sleeps with a virgin who's engaged, and they do it in the city—
22.24: Both of them gotta be stoned. The man 'cause he disrespected another man's wife, and the woman 'cause she ain't cry out for help.
22.25: But if it happens in the countryside, only the man dies—
22.26: The woman ain't done nothing wrong. She was attacked and couldn't call for help.
22.27: It's like when somebody attacks and kills their neighbor—the woman in the field was just minding her business. She screamed, but wasn't nobody around to help her.
22.28: If a man sleeps with a virgin who ain't engaged, and they get caught—
22.29: He gotta pay her father 50 shekels and marry her. He can't ever divorce her.
22.30: A man must not sleep with his father's wife or dishonor his father's bed.

23.1: Anybody who's been castrated or mutilated can't be part of the Lord's assembly.
23.2: A child born outside of marriage can't be in the Lord's assembly—even up to ten generations later.
23.3: No Ammonite or Moabite can join the Lord's assembly—not even ten generations down the line.
23.4: Why? 'Cause when y'all came out of Egypt, they ain't offer y'all food or water. Instead, they hired Balaam, son of Beor, to put a curse on y'all.
23.5: But God flipped the script! He ain't listen to Balaam—instead, He turned the curse into a blessing, 'cause the Lord loves y'all.
23.6: Don't ever seek peace or prosperity from the Ammonites or Moabites. Forever.
23.7: But don't hate the Edomites— they family. And don't hate the Egyptians, 'cause y'all were foreigners in their land once.
23.8: By the third generation, their kids can enter the Lord's assembly.
23.9: When y'all at war, stay clean— don't mess with anything wicked.
23.10: If somebody gets unclean overnight, he gotta go outside the camp and stay out till the evening.
23.11: At sunset, he can wash up and come back in.
23.12: Have a designated bathroom area outside the camp.
23.13: Keep a shovel with you, dig a hole, and cover your waste.
23.14: Why? 'Cause the Lord walks among y'all, fighting for you. Keep the camp holy, so He don't turn away.
23.15: If a slave escapes and comes to you, don't send them back to their master.
23.16: Let them live free wherever they choose— don't oppress them.
23.17: No Israelite woman should be a temple prostitute, and no Israelite man should be out here selling himself either.
23.18: Don't bring prostitute money or dirty earnings into the Lord's house. The Lord don't accept dirty money.
23.19: Don't charge interest on loans to your fellow Israelite— not on money, food, or anything else.
23.20: You can charge interest to foreigners, but not your own people. If you obey, the Lord will bless you in the land He's giving you.
23.21: If you make a vow to the Lord, don't play around—pay it fast. He gon' hold you to it, and if you delay, that's a sin.
23.22: If you don't make a vow, you ain't sinning. But if you say it, you better do it.
23.23: If it comes out your mouth, keep your word— you made that promise voluntarily to the Lord.
23.24: If you walk into your neighbor's vineyard, you can eat some grapes, but don't take none to go.
23.25: If you go through their grain field, you can pluck some heads to eat, but don't use a sickle to start harvesting their crops.

24.1: If a man marries a woman but later decides she ain't what he wants—because he found something in her that ain't right—he can write her a divorce paper, hand it to her, and send her out.
24.2: If she leaves, remarries, and becomes another man's wife,
24.3: And if that second husband also divorces her or dies,
24.4: She can't go back to her first husband. That's nasty in the Lord's eyes, and y'all ain't tryna bring sin on the land He gave you.
24.5: If a man just got married, he ain't gotta go to war or take on major responsibilities for a whole year. He needs to stay home and make his wife happy.
24.6: Don't take a man's millstone (the thing he grinds his grain with) as a loan guarantee. That's like taking his whole livelihood.
24.7: If somebody kidnaps a fellow Israelite, mistreats them, or sells them into slavery, that person gotta die. Y'all gotta get rid of that kind of evil.
24.8: If there's a disease outbreak like leprosy, follow whatever instructions the priests give you. They know what they doing.
24.9: Remember what happened to Miriam when she caught that disease on the way out of Egypt!
24.10: If you lend somebody something, don't barge into their house to get your collateral.
24.11: Wait outside and let them bring it to you.
24.12: If the borrower is struggling, don't keep his pledge overnight.
24.13: Give it back before the sun sets so he can sleep in peace. That's the righteous thing to do in the Lord's eyes.
24.14: Don't cheat or mistreat a poor worker— whether they Israelite or a foreigner living in your land.
24.15: Pay them their wages every day, before the sun goes down. They need that money to survive, and if they cry out to God, He gon' come for you.
24.16: Parents won't be punished for their kids' sins, and kids won't be punished for their parents' sins. Everybody is responsible for their own wrongdoing.
24.17: Don't cheat a foreigner or an orphan, and don't take a widow's last bit of clothing as collateral.
24.18: Remember—y'all used to be slaves in Egypt, and God rescued y'all. That's why He commands y'all to be fair.
24.19: If you forget a bundle of wheat in the field during harvest, don't go back for it. Leave it for the foreigners, orphans, and widows—God gon' bless you for it.
24.20: When you harvest your olive trees, don't go over them a second time. Leave what's left for those in need.
24.21: Same thing with your grapevines—don't pick them clean. Leave some for the poor.
24.22: And don't forget—you used to be slaves in Egypt. That's why God commands you to do this.

25.1: If two men got a dispute and take it to court, the judges gotta decide the case— justifying the innocent and condemning the guilty.
25.2: If the guilty man deserves a beating, the judge will have him lay down and be whipped according to how bad his crime was.
25.3: But don't give him more than 40 lashes, or else he'll be humiliated in front of everybody.
25.4: Don't muzzle an ox while it's working, treading out grain. Let it eat while it works.
25.5: If two brothers live together and one dies without a son, his widow can't marry outside the family. His brother must marry her and take care of her.
25.6: The first son they have will carry the dead brother's name so his legacy don't disappear in Israel.
25.7: But if the brother refuses to marry her, she gotta go to the city elders and say, 'My husband's brother won't keep the family name going.'
25.8: The elders will call him out and talk to him, but if he still refuses—
25.9: The widow will remove his sandal, spit in his face, and say, 'This what happens to a man who won't build up his brother's house.'
25.10: From then on, his family gon' be called, 'The house of the man who got his sandal removed.'
25.11: If two men fighting, and the wife of one jumps in to grab the other man's privates to stop the fight—
25.12: She gotta lose her hand. No mercy on that.
25.13: Don't keep dishonest scales in your bag— one heavy and one light to cheat people.
25.14: Don't keep different measures in your house— one big and one small.
25.15: Use honest and fair weights and measures, so you can live long in the land the Lord is giving you.
25.16: Anybody who cheats like that is disgusting to the Lord.
25.17: Remember what Amalek did when y'all were leaving Egypt.
25.18: They ambushed y'all from behind, attacking the weak and weary— and they ain't respect God.
25.19: So when the Lord gives y'all peace in the land, wipe out Amalek's memory forever. Don't forget this.

26.1: When y'all finally settle in the land the Lord is giving you, take possession and make it home.
26.2: Then gather the first crops from what the land produces, put them in a basket, and take them to the place the Lord chooses for His name to dwell.
26.3: Go to the priest on duty and say, 'I'm here to declare before the Lord that I made it to the land He promised our ancestors.'
26.4: The priest gon' take your basket and place it before the altar of the Lord.
26.5: Then you gotta say before the Lord: 'My ancestor was a wandering Aramean who barely made it. He went to Egypt with just a few folks, but over time, we became a mighty nation.
26.6: But the Egyptians treated us bad— they oppressed us and made us slaves.
26.7: So we cried out to the Lord, and He heard us—He saw our suffering and struggle.
26.8: Then He brought us out with power— using signs, wonders, and a mighty hand.
26.9: Now He brought us to this land, a place flowing with milk and honey.
26.10: So here I am, bringing the firstfruits of the land You gave me.
26.11: Place it before the Lord and worship. Celebrate the blessings He gave you—you, the Levites, and the foreigners among you.
26.12: Every third year—the year of tithing— set aside your tithe and make sure the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows get what they need so they can eat and be full.
26.13: Then say before the Lord, 'I have given away the holy tithe as You commanded—to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow. I ain't held back.
26.14: I ain't touched it while mourning, used it improperly, or given any for the dead. I obeyed Your commands, Lord.
26.15: Look down from heaven, Your holy place, and bless Israel and the land You gave us— the land flowing with milk and honey, just like You promised.
26.16: Today, the Lord is commanding y'all to follow His laws and rules. So y'all need to be serious and obey with all your heart and soul.
26.17: Today, y'all declared that the Lord is your God, and that y'all gon' walk in His ways, keep His commands, and obey His voice.
26.18: And today, the Lord declared that y'all are His special people, just like He promised—as long as y'all keep His commandments.
