26.19: He gon' set y'all above all nations, giving y'all praise, fame, and honor. Y'all gon' be His holy people, just like He said.

27.1: Moses and the elders told the people: 'Keep all these commandments I'm giving y'all today.'
27.2: When y'all cross the Jordan into the land the Lord is giving you, set up large stones and cover them with lime.
27.3: Write all the words of this law on them once you cross over into the land the Lord promised—a land flowing with milk and honey.
27.4: After crossing the Jordan, put these stones on Mount Ebal and coat them with lime, just like I told y'all.
27.5: Build an altar to the Lord on Mount Ebal using uncut stones. No iron tools should touch them.
27.6: Use whole stones to build the altar and offer burnt sacrifices to the Lord.
27.7: Make peace offerings, eat there, and celebrate before the Lord.
27.8: Write these laws out clearly on the stones.
27.9: Then Moses and the Levite priests spoke to Israel: 'Listen up! Today y'all officially the Lord's people.'
27.10: So obey Him, follow His commands, and keep all His laws I'm giving y'all today.
27.11: That same day, Moses gave the people these instructions:
27.12: When y'all cross over, these tribes gon' stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
27.13: And these tribes gon' stand on Mount Ebal to pronounce curses: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
27.14: Then the Levites gon' speak loud and clear to all of Israel:
27.15: 'Cursed is the one who makes idols in secret— false gods, hand-crafted, and disgusting to the Lord.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.16: 'Cursed is the one who disrespects their mama or daddy.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.17: 'Cursed is the one who moves their neighbor's property line.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.18: 'Cursed is the one who misleads blind folks, making them lose their way.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.19: 'Cursed is the one who twists justice against foreigners, orphans, and widows.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.20: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his father's wife, disrespecting his father's bed.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.21: 'Cursed is the one who has sex with animals.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.22: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his sister—whether they got the same father or mother.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.23: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his mother-in-law.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.24: 'Cursed is the one who attacks their neighbor in secret.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.25: 'Cursed is the one who takes bribes to kill an innocent person.' And everybody says, "Amen!"
27.26: 'Cursed is the one who don't uphold all these laws and live by them.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

28.1: If y'all fully obey the Lord, doing everything He commands, He gon' lift y'all up above all the nations on earth.
28.2: All these blessings gon' come on y'all and overtake y'all, just for listening to the Lord's voice.
28.3: Blessed in the city, blessed in the country.
28.4: Your kids gon' be blessed, your crops gon' be blessed, your livestock gon' multiply.
28.5: Your food supply—your basket and your kneading bowl— gon' be full and blessed.
28.6: Blessed when you come in, blessed when you go out.
28.7: The Lord gon' make your enemies scatter. They might come at you one way, but they gon' run away in seven different directions.
28.8: God gon' bless your storehouses and everything you put your hands on. He gon' bless the land He's giving you.
28.9: He gon' set y'all apart as His holy people, as long as y'all follow His commands and walk in His ways.
28.10: Everybody gon' see that y'all belong to the Lord, and they gon' be scared of y'all.
28.11: The Lord gon' overflow your blessings— your kids, your animals, and your land gon' produce plenty.
28.12: He gon' open up the heavens for y'all, sending rain at the right time and blessing everything you do. Y'all gon' lend to nations but never borrow.
28.13: God gon' make you the head, not the tail. You gon' be on top, not underneath—but only if you listen and obey.
28.14: Don't stray to the left or right. Don't go chasing after other gods—stay on the path He gave you.
28.15: But if y'all ignore the Lord's voice and refuse to follow His commands, these curses gon' come on y'all and overtake you.
28.16: Cursed in the city, cursed in the country.
28.17: Cursed food supply—your basket and your kneading bowl gon' be empty.
28.18: Cursed kids, cursed land, cursed livestock—everything gon' struggle.
28.19: Cursed when you come in, cursed when you go out.
28.20: The Lord gon' send confusion and destruction in everything you do, 'til you completely fail, all because you turned away from Him.
28.21: Disease gon' stick to you 'til it wipes you out. You ain't even gon' make it to the land you tryna possess.
28.22: He gon' hit you with fevers, inflammation, drought, scorching heat, and mildew— these things ain't gon' stop 'til you done.
28.23: The sky gon' be like bronze over your head, and the ground gon' be like iron. No rain, no harvest.
28.24: Instead of rain, dust and ashes gon' fall from the sky 'til you completely destroyed.
28.25: Your enemies gon' tear you up. You'll run at them one way, but end up fleeing in seven different directions. All the nations gon' look at you like a joke.
28.26: Your dead bodies gon' be food for birds and wild animals— and ain't nobody gon' be there to chase them off.
28.27: God gon' hit you with boils like He did in Egypt— sores, rashes, infections that can't be healed.
28.28: He gon' strike you with madness, blindness, and total confusion.
28.29: In the middle of the day, you gon' be stumbling around like it's midnight. Nothing you try gon' work out, and people gon' rob and oppress you nonstop, with nobody to help.
28.30: You gon' get engaged to a woman, but another man gon' sleep with her. You'll build a house, but never live in it. You'll plant a vineyard, but won't get to enjoy the grapes.
28.31: Your ox gon' be taken and slaughtered right in front of you, but you won't get to eat none of it. Your donkey gon' be snatched away and never returned. Your sheep gon' be handed over to your enemies, and ain't nobody gon' save them.
28.32: Your sons and daughters gon' be taken by another nation, and you gon' be helpless, watching them go. Your eyes gon' fail from crying all day, but you won't have the strength to stop it.
28.33: A nation you don't even know gon' eat all your crops and take everything you worked for. You gon' be oppressed and crushed nonstop.
28.34: It's gon' drive you crazy seeing all this happen.
28.35: The Lord gon' hit you with painful boils, from your feet to your head, and ain't no healing from it.
28.36: He gon' take you and your king and send y'all to a land you never knew. There, y'all gon' be forced to worship false gods—wood and stone.
28.37: People gon' look at y'all like a joke, a proverb, a lesson—everywhere the Lord scatters you.
28.38: You gon' plant plenty of seeds, but barely harvest anything— 'cause locusts gon' eat up your crops.
28.39: You gon' plant vineyards and take care of them, but you ain't drinking no wine— 'cause worms gon' eat the grapes.
28.40: You'll have olive trees everywhere, but you ain't using that oil— 'cause the olives gon' fall off before they ripen.
28.41: You'll have sons and daughters, but they ain't staying with you— 'cause they gon' be taken into captivity.
28.42: Locusts gon' eat up every tree and crop in your land.
28.43: The foreigners living among y'all gon' keep rising higher and higher, while you keep falling lower and lower.
28.44: They gon' be lending to you, but you won't lend to them. They gon' be the head, and you gon' be the tail.
28.45: Every one of these curses gon' come after you, chase you down, and overtake you 'til you destroyed— all because you ain't listen to the Lord or follow His commands.
28.46: These curses gon' be a sign and a warning for you and your descendants forever.
28.47: Since you ain't serve the Lord with joy when He blessed you with everything—
28.48: Now you gon' serve your enemies, in hunger, thirst, and poverty. They gon' put a yoke of iron on your neck 'til you completely destroyed.
28.49: The Lord gon' bring a nation against you from far away— flying in fast like an eagle. They gon' speak a language you don't understand.
28.50: They ain't gon' care about your elders, and they ain't gon' have mercy on your children.
28.51: They gon' take everything—your livestock, your crops— 'til you got nothing left. They gon' wipe you out.
28.52: They gon' trap you inside your own cities, tearing down all the walls you thought would protect you. They gon' besiege you everywhere in the land the Lord gave you.
28.53: You gon' be so desperate, you'll eat your own children— the sons and daughters the Lord gave you. That's how bad the siege gon' be.
28.54: The softest, most refined man among you gon' turn cold, even toward his own family.
28.55: He won't share food with his own wife and kids, 'cause he barely got enough for himself.
28.56: Even the most delicate woman, who wouldn't even step on the ground barefoot, gon' turn against her own husband, son, and daughter.
28.57: She gon' secretly eat her own newborns and the afterbirth, just to survive. That's how bad the siege gon' get.
28.58: If y'all don't take this law seriously, if y'all don't respect the Lord's great and powerful name—
28.59: The Lord gon' hit y'all and your descendants with plagues— terrible, long-lasting diseases.
28.60: He gon' bring back all the sicknesses of Egypt, the ones y'all feared the most, and they gon' stick to you.
28.61: Every sickness and plague— even the ones not written in this Book of the Law— the Lord gon' hit you with them 'til you completely destroyed.
28.62: Y'all used to be as numerous as the stars in the sky, but now? Y'all gon' be reduced to just a few. All 'cause y'all ain't listen to the Lord.
28.63: Just like He used to take joy in blessing y'all and making y'all multiply, now He gon' take joy in wiping y'all out. He gon' pluck y'all right off the land He gave you.
28.64: The Lord gon' scatter y'all all over the earth— from one end to the other. Wherever you go, you gon' be forced to serve other gods, gods of wood and stone that neither you nor your ancestors ever knew.
28.65: Ain't gon' be no peace for you anywhere. No rest, no stability. The Lord gon' fill your heart with fear, your eyes with sorrow, and your soul with deep anxiety.
28.66: You gon' be living on edge, never knowing if you gon' survive the next day. Fear gon' haunt you day and night.
28.67: Every morning, you gon' wish it was nighttime. Every night, you gon' wish it was morning. That's how scared and broken y'all gon' be.
28.68: The Lord gon' send y'all back to Egypt in ships— even though He said y'all would never go back that way. And there, y'all gon' be put up for sale as slaves to your enemies— but ain't nobody even gon' want to buy you.

29.1: These are the words of the covenant the Lord told Moses to make with Israel in Moab— this is on top of the one He made at Mount Horeb.
29.2: Moses gathered everybody and said: 'Y'all saw with your own eyes everything the Lord did in Egypt—how He took down Pharaoh, his officials, and his whole land.
29.3: Y'all saw the great trials, the signs, and the wonders.
29.4: But even now, the Lord ain't given y'all the understanding, eyes to see, or ears to hear what it all really means.
29.5: I led y'all in this wilderness for 40 years— and guess what? Your clothes ain't wear out, and neither did your sandals.
29.6: Y'all ain't had bread to eat or wine to drink, so y'all would know that I am the Lord your God.
29.7: When y'all got here, Sihon (king of Heshbon) and Og (king of Bashan) came to fight— but we beat them.
29.8: We took their land and gave it to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh's tribe.
29.9: So keep this covenant and obey it, so y'all can prosper in everything y'all do.
29.10: Today, all of y'all stand before the Lord— your leaders, elders, officers, all the men of Israel,
29.11: Your kids, your wives, and even the foreigners among y'all— from the ones chopping wood to the ones fetching water.
29.12: This is so y'all can enter into this covenant with the Lord today, the agreement He's making with y'all.
29.13: He's making y'all His people today, just like He promised your ancestors—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
29.14: This covenant ain't just for y'all standing here today—
29.15: It's for future generations too, the ones who ain't even here yet.
29.16: Y'all remember living in Egypt, and how we passed through other nations on the way here.
29.17: Y'all saw their nasty idols— statues made of wood, stone, silver, and gold.
29.18: So don't let anybody among y'all—man, woman, family, or tribe— turn away from the Lord today to follow these false gods.
29.19: Don't let nobody hear these warnings and think, 'I'll be fine, I'm gon' do what I want.' That's like a drunk fool thinking he safe like a sober man.
29.20: The Lord ain't gon' let that slide. His anger gon' burn against that person, and every curse in this book gon' fall on them.
29.21: The Lord gon' separate them from the whole nation and hit them with all the curses written in this Book of the Law.
29.22: In the future, when your kids and foreigners come through and see the disaster and sickness in this land—
29.23: When they see the land burned up with sulfur and salt, with nothing growing— just like what happened to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim when the Lord destroyed them—
29.24: They gon' ask, 'Why did the Lord do all this? Why is He so angry?'
29.25: And people gon' answer, 'Cause they broke the Lord's covenant, the one He made with them when He freed them from Egypt.
29.26: Instead of worshiping Him, they chased after false gods— ones they ain't never known, ones the Lord never gave them.
29.27: So the Lord's anger burned against the land, bringing down every curse written in this book.
29.28: He uprooted them from their land in His anger and threw them into another country— and that's where they at now.
29.29: The secret things belong to the Lord, but what He reveals? That's for us and our children forever, so we can follow His law.

30.1: One day, when all these blessings and curses I told y'all about come true, and y'all remember them while living in whatever nation the Lord sent you to—
30.2: If y'all turn back to the Lord, listen to His voice, and follow His commands— you and your kids, with all your heart and soul—
30.3: Then the Lord gon' bring y'all back from captivity. He gon' have mercy on y'all and gather y'all from every nation where He scattered you.
30.4: Even if some of y'all are at the farthest corner of the earth, the Lord gon' bring y'all back.
30.5: He gon' bring y'all back to the land He promised your ancestors, and you gon' take possession of it. He gon' bless you even more than your fathers.
30.6: The Lord gon' change your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so y'all can love Him with all your heart and soul, and truly live.
30.7: And all those curses? The Lord gon' put them on your enemies instead—on the ones who hated and oppressed you.
30.8: Then y'all gon' obey the Lord again, following all His commands like He told you to.
30.9: The Lord gon' bless everything you do— your kids, your livestock, your crops. He gon' take joy in blessing you, just like He did your ancestors.
30.10: But that's only if y'all listen to His voice, keep His commandments, and turn back to Him with all your heart and soul.
30.11: This command I'm giving you ain't hard to understand. It ain't some deep mystery.
30.12: It ain't up in heaven, so you don't gotta ask, 'Who gon' go up there and bring it down so we can hear it and do it?'
30.13: It ain't across the ocean either, so you don't gotta ask, 'Who gon' go get it and bring it back so we can hear and do it?'
30.14: Nah, the word is right here— in your mouth and in your heart—so you can live by it.
30.15: Today, I'm laying it out for y'all— life and good, or death and evil. The choice is yours.
30.16: If you love the Lord, walk in His ways, and keep His commands, then y'all gon' live, multiply, and be blessed in the land you about to take over.
30.17: But if you turn away, refuse to listen, and start worshiping other gods—
30.18: I'm telling you right now—you gon' be destroyed. You ain't gon' last long in the land across the Jordan.
30.19: I'm calling heaven and earth as witnesses today: I put life and death, blessings and curses in front of y'all. So choose life, so you and your kids can live!
30.20: Love the Lord, listen to His voice, and stay close to Him. He is your life and the key to your future. That's how y'all gon' live long in the land He promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

31.1: Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel:
31.2: 'I'm 120 years old today. I can't move like I used to, and the Lord already told me, "You ain't crossing this Jordan."
31.3: But the Lord gon' go before y'all. He gon' wipe out these nations, and y'all gon' take their land. Joshua gon' lead y'all across, just like the Lord said.
31.4: The Lord gon' do to these nations just like He did to Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings—He destroyed them completely.
31.5: He gon' hand them over to y'all, and y'all gotta handle them just like I commanded.
31.6: Be strong and courageous. Don't be scared of them. The Lord your God is with you—He ain't never gon' leave you or forsake you.
31.7: Then Moses called Joshua in front of everybody and told him, 'Be strong and courageous! You gotta lead these people into the land the Lord promised their ancestors.
31.8: The Lord Himself is going ahead of you. He gon' be with you—He won't abandon you. Don't be scared or discouraged!
31.9: Moses wrote down the law and gave it to the priests, the Levites who carried the Ark of the Covenant, and to the elders of Israel.
31.10: He commanded them, 'Every seven years, during the Year of Release, at the Feast of Tabernacles—
31.11: When all of Israel gathers before the Lord, y'all gotta read this law out loud to everybody.
31.12: Gather the men, women, kids, and even the foreigners living among y'all, so they can hear, learn, and respect the Lord's commands.
31.13: Even the next generation—who ain't heard this before—needs to learn to fear the Lord while y'all live in the land y'all about to take over.'
31.14: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Your time is almost up. Call Joshua, and both of y'all come to the Tabernacle so I can officially appoint him.'
31.15: The Lord showed up at the Tabernacle in a pillar of cloud, standing above the entrance.
31.16: Then the Lord told Moses, 'You about to die, and after you gone, these people gon' turn their backs on Me. They gon' start worshiping other gods in the new land, breaking My covenant.'
31.17: That's gon' make Me angry. I'm gon' turn My back on them and let them get destroyed. They gon' suffer so bad, they gon' say, "Is this happening 'cause God ain't with us no more?"
31.18: But I ain't gon' listen to them, 'cause they gon' be deep in sin, chasing after other gods.
31.19: So write down this song and teach it to Israel. Let it be a witness against them.
31.20: When I bless them with the land of milk and honey, and they get comfortable, they gon' forget Me and start worshiping false gods.
31.21: When disasters hit them, this song gon' be a reminder. Their descendants ain't gon' forget it, 'cause I already know how they act—even before they step foot in the land.
31.22: So Moses wrote the song that same day and taught it to Israel.
31.23: Then the Lord gave Joshua his orders: 'Be strong and courageous! You gon' lead Israel into the land I promised, and I'm gon' be with you.'
31.24: When Moses finished writing all the words of this law,
31.25: He told the Levites who carried the Ark of the Covenant—
31.26: 'Take this Book of the Law and put it beside the Ark. Let it be a witness against y'all.
31.27: I already know how rebellious y'all are. If y'all act this way while I'm still alive, what y'all gon' do after I'm gone?
31.28: Gather all the elders and officials. I got some final words to say, and I'm calling heaven and earth as my witnesses.
31.29: I already know what's gon' happen after I die. Y'all gon' turn away from the Lord and do evil, making Him angry. Y'all gon' bring disaster on yourselves in the future.
31.30: Then Moses stood before all of Israel and spoke the words of the song from beginning to end.

32.1: Listen up, heavens, 'cause I'm 'bout to speak! Earth, pay attention to my words!
32.2: Let my teachings fall like rain, my words settle like morning dew—like showers watering the grass.
32.3: I'm lifting up the Lord's name— give Him the honor He deserves!
32.4: He's the Rock—His work is flawless! Everything He does is just, He's a God of truth, no corruption in Him.
32.5: But these people done messed themselves up. They ain't acting like His children—they a twisted, messed-up generation.
32.6: How y'all gon' treat the Lord like this? Acting foolish and ungrateful! Ain't He your Father, the One who bought you? He made you and set you up!
32.7: Think back to the old days, remember what happened generations ago. Ask your elders, they'll tell you what's up.
32.8: When the Most High divided the land among the nations, when He spread out the sons of Adam, He set up the boundaries based on His chosen people, Israel.
32.9: But Israel? That's God's special portion. Jacob is His own inheritance.
32.10: He found them in a dry, wild place— a desert full of chaos. He surrounded them, taught them, kept them safe like they were His most prized possession.
32.11: Like an eagle watching over its babies, hovering, carrying them on its wings—
32.12: That's how the Lord led Israel— no false gods, just Him.
32.13: He lifted them up to high places, blessed them with the best food—honey from rocks, oil from stone.
32.14: Milk from cattle, the finest meats, the best wheat, and the richest wine.
32.15: But Jeshurun (Israel) got too comfortable. They got fat, thick, and lazy—then turned their back on God. They forgot who made them!
32.16: They made God jealous by worshiping false gods, doing disgusting things that made Him angry.
32.17: They started sacrificing to demons, not the true God— to gods they never knew, new gods their ancestors never heard of.
32.18: They forgot about the Rock who made them. They ignored the God who gave them life.
32.19: When the Lord saw this, He had enough. He rejected them, 'cause they made Him angry.
32.20: He said, 'I'm gon' turn My back on them. Let's see how they end up. They a messed-up generation—ain't got no loyalty.
32.21: They made Me jealous with fake gods, so I'ma make them jealous with a people who ain't even a real nation. They made Me angry, so I'ma use a foolish people to make them mad.
32.22: My anger burns like a fire, reaching all the way to hell. It's gon' consume the earth and burn the mountains to their foundations.
32.23: I'ma send disaster after disaster on them. I got arrows, and I'ma use 'em all.
32.24: They gon' waste away from hunger, be eaten up by disease, and torn apart by wild animals and deadly snakes.
32.25: The sword gon' strike 'em down outside, and inside they gon' be full of terror—young and old, babies and the elderly, nobody spared.
32.26: I could've said, 'I'ma wipe them out completely, erase them from history.'
32.27: But I held back, 'cause I ain't tryna let their enemies get cocky. I ain't want them thinking, 'We did this ourselves, not the Lord.'
32.28: Israel acting like they ain't got no sense, no wisdom at all.
32.29: If only they were wise enough to understand what's coming, to think about how this all gon' end.
32.30: Ain't no way one enemy chases a thousand of y'all, and two run off ten thousand—unless the Lord let it happen.
32.31: Their gods ain't nothing like our God. Even our enemies can see that!
32.32: They ain't nothing but the vine of Sodom, growing from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poison, their fruit is bitter.
32.33: Their wine is snake venom, straight-up deadly.
32.34: Y'all don't think I see all this? I got it stored up, waiting for the right time.
32.35: Vengeance is Mine! Payback coming, and when they slip, it's gon' be bad. Their disaster coming quick!
32.36: The Lord gon' judge His people, but He gon' have compassion when He sees they completely powerless, no one left to fight.
32.37: Then He gon' ask, 'Where them fake gods at now? The ones y'all was trusting in?
32.38: Where the gods that took y'all's offerings? The ones y'all poured drink offerings for? Tell them to help y'all now!
32.39: But now y'all see—I'm the only God. Ain't no one else but Me. I got the power to kill and bring life, to wound and heal. Ain't nobody who can escape My hands.
32.40: I lift My hand to heaven and swear— I live forever!
32.41: When I sharpen My sword for judgment, I'ma pay back every enemy that hated Me.
32.42: My arrows gon' be drunk off blood, and My sword gon' devour flesh—even from the enemy leaders.
32.43: Rejoice, nations! 'Cause the Lord gon' take revenge for His people. He gon' punish His enemies and restore His land and His people.
32.44: Moses and Joshua son of Nun stood before the people and spoke every word of this song.
32.46: He told them, 'Take these words seriously. Teach them to your children. Make sure they live by them.
32.47: This ain't just some empty words— this is y'all's life! Obey them, and y'all gon' live long in the land y'all 'bout to take over.
32.48: That same day, the Lord spoke to Moses.
32.49: He said, 'Go up Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, across from Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan—I'm giving it to Israel.
32.50: Then you gon' die up there and join your ancestors, just like Aaron died on Mount Hor.
32.51: This is 'cause you disrespected Me at Meribah Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin. You ain't honor Me in front of the people.
32.52: You gon' see the land, but you ain't stepping foot in it. That's the land I'm giving to Israel.

33.1: This is the blessing Moses, the man of God, gave Israel before he passed.
33.2: He said, 'The Lord showed up at Sinai, shined His light from Seir, came strong from Mount Paran, rolling deep with ten thousand angels. His right hand held a fiery law for His people.
33.3: He loves His people! All His followers in His hands, sitting at His feet, learning from Him.
33.4: Moses gave us God's law, our inheritance as the people of Jacob.
33.5: He was King over Israel (Jeshurun) when all the leaders and tribes gathered together.
33.6: Reuben, may your tribe survive, and don't let your numbers get too low.
33.7: For Judah: 'Lord, hear Judah's voice! Bring him back to his people. Let him have strength in his hands, and help him against his enemies.'
33.8: For Levi: 'Lord, let the Urim and Thummim stay with Your holy one—the one You tested at Massah and Meribah.
33.9: Levi stood firm, even against family— they put God first, kept His word, and stayed true to the covenant.
33.10: They gon' teach Jacob and Israel Your laws. They'll burn incense before You and bring offerings to Your altar.
33.11: Lord, bless Levi's work, accept what he does for You. Strike down anyone who rises against him!
33.12: For Benjamin: 'The one the Lord loves gon' live safe with Him. The Lord gon' shelter him all day long, carrying him on His shoulders.'
33.13: For Joseph: 'His land gon' be blessed by the Lord— heaven's dew, deep underground waters.
33.14: The best crops from the sun, and the best harvest every season.
33.15: The richest land from ancient mountains, the finest treasures from everlasting hills.
33.16: Everything good from the earth, along with God's favor. Let this blessing fall on Joseph, the one set apart from his brothers.
33.17: He's strong like a firstborn bull, with horns like a wild ox. With them, he gon' push nations all the way to the ends of the earth. That's Ephraim's ten thousands and Manasseh's thousands.'
33.18: For Zebulun and Issachar: 'Zebulun, be joyful when you go out! Issachar, be blessed in your tents!'
33.19: They gon' call nations to worship, offering righteous sacrifices. They'll enjoy the riches of the seas and treasures buried in the sand.
33.20: For Gad: 'Bless the one who expands Gad's land! He's fierce like a lion, ripping through arms and skulls.
33.21: Gad claimed his territory early, got land reserved for leaders. He led the people and carried out God's justice.
33.22: For Dan: 'Dan is like a young lion, leaping from Bashan to strike.'
33.23: For Naphtali: 'Naphtali is full of God's favor, overflowing with blessings! Take possession of the west and the south.'
33.24: For Asher: 'Asher is blessed above all his brothers. His people love him, and he walks in oil (wealth and prosperity).
33.25: His feet gon' be as strong as iron and bronze. His strength gon' last as long as his days.
33.26: Ain't nobody like the God of Israel! He rides through the heavens to help you, soaring on the clouds in glory.
33.27: The eternal God is your safe place. His everlasting arms hold you up. He gon' push out your enemies and tell you to destroy them.
33.28: Israel gon' live in safety, with Jacob's descendants flourishing in a land of grain and wine. The skies gon' drop dew on them.
33.29: You blessed, Israel! Ain't nobody like you— saved by the Lord, protected by His shield, victorious by His sword. Your enemies gon' bow before you, and you gon' stomp on their strongholds.

34.1: Moses climbed up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, all the way to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. The Lord showed him the whole land—Gilead all the way to Dan,
34.2: Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and all of Judah, reaching the Western Sea.
34.3: He showed him the South, the plains, the Valley of Jericho (the city of palm trees), and all the way to Zoar.
34.4: Then the Lord told him, 'This the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying I'd give it to their descendants. I'm letting you see it with your own eyes, but you ain't crossing over.
34.5: So Moses, the Lord's servant, died right there in Moab, just like the Lord said.
34.6: The Lord Himself buried Moses in a valley in Moab, across from Beth Peor, but nobody knows exactly where his grave is to this day.
34.7: Moses was 120 years old when he died, but his eyesight was still sharp, and he still had his strength.
34.8: The Israelites mourned for Moses for 30 days in the plains of Moab. Then the time of grieving was over.
34.9: Joshua, son of Nun, was full of wisdom, 'cause Moses had laid hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did what the Lord commanded through Moses.
34.10: Ain't never been another prophet in Israel like Moses— the one the Lord spoke to face to face.
34.11: He did signs and wonders in Egypt, in front of Pharaoh, his officials, and all his people.
34.12: With God's mighty power, Moses did things that shook the world— miracles that left Israel in awe.
